newsitem.title: USA: Mobil to buy Exxon's Kenya marketing.
newsitem.headline: Mobil to buy Exxon's Kenya marketing.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Friday it agreed to purchase Exxon Corp's marketing operations in Kenya, noting the purchase marks Mobil's re-entry into Kenya after a 10-year absence.
It said the operations include lubricants blending and marketing, plus marketing for fuels, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) and chemicals. Terms of the transaction were not disclosed.
Exxon's current market share in Kenya is about 12.5 percent, or 100 million gallons of fuels and lubricants per year, Mobil said.

It said the main assets involved in the acquisition include 80 retail outlets, a 240,000-barrel import/export terminal which will enhance Mobil's ability to supply other countries in East Africa, a 125,000 barrel lubricant oil blending plant and a liquefied petroleum gas filling plant, the latter three all in Mombasa.
In addition, Mobil will acquire refueling service facilities at the Nairobi and Mombasa airports.
Mobil currently markets 120,000 barrels per day of fuels and lubricant products in 41 countries in Africa.
